feedback.problem:
The center of the hyperbola $9{y}^{2}-16{x}^{2}-72y=-108$ is$\,\,($
{{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}
$).$
feedback.worked_solution:
The equation of a vertical hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in the above form, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}9{y}^{2}-16{x}^{2}-72y & =-108 \\ 9{y}^{2}-72y-16{x}^{2} & =-108 \\ 9[{y}^{2}-8y]-16[{x}^{2}] & =-108 \\ 9[(y-4)^{2}-16]-16{x}^{2} & =-108 \\ 9(y-4)^{2}-144-16{x}^{2} & =-108 \\ 9(y-4)^{2}-16{x}^{2} & =-108+144 \\ 9(y-4)^{2}-16{x}^{2} & =36 \\ \frac{(y-4)^{2}}{4}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{9/4} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the center of the hyperbola is $(\,0,4\,).$
